page_numbering_note: PDF page numbers are used throughout this inventory (the ===PAGE n=== markers). The report's own printed folio runs 4 lower: PDF 5 = printed page 1, and the table of contents on PDF pages 3-4 uses the printed numbers. PDF pages 2 and 186 have no text layer at all.

tables.name: Table of contents
tables.what_it_is: Two-column contents list mapping each department report and financial statement to a printed page range; also records which boards filed 'No Report Submitted'.
tables.grain: One report/section and its printed page range

tables.notes: Useful as an independent index of what SHOULD be in the book. Two entries do not deliver: 'Trust and Stabilization Funds Held by Other Banks Page 33' has a heading on PDF p37 but no data under it, and one entry reads 'Conservation Commission Pages 44-43' (reversed). Six bodies are listed as 'No Report Submitted': Cultural Council, Green Communities Committee, Historical Commission, Housing Authority, Capital Planning Report, Master Planning Steering Committee.

tables.name: Town profile fact box
tables.what_it_is: A handful of headline town statistics printed as a banner above narrative history.
tables.layout: Centred label-dash-value lines, badly interleaved by the text extractor
tables.notes: Values: YEAR INCORPORATED-1728; REGISTERED VOTERS- 9,240; FY'25 TAX RATE- $14.36; ANNUAL TOWN ELECTION- 3RD SATURDAY IN MAY; ANNUAL TOWN MEETING- 1ST SATURDAY IN MAY; TOTAL AREA- 26.63 MILES. Note the registered-voter count here (9,240) does not match the election tally sheet on p171 (9,608).

tables.name: State and federal elected officials directory

tables.layout: Two side-by-side address blocks per row, under office headings
tables.notes: Two-column layout collapses in the text dump — lines interleave the left and right officeholder.

tables.name: Elected town officials with term-expiry years
tables.what_it_is: Every elected board and office, its statutory size and term length, and each sitting member with the year their term expires. Vacancies are counted explicitly.

tables.notes: Boards covered: Assessors, Board of Health, Select Board, Cemetery Commission, Constable, Housing Authority, Library Trustees, Moderator, Parks Commission, Planning Board, School Committee, Sewer Commission, Town Clerk, Trust Fund Commission. Vacancy lines read '1 Vacancy'. School Committee is described as '(5 members)' here though the Lunenburg Profile narrative on p9 says an elected seven-member School Committee — a real internal inconsistency.

tables.name: Appointed town officials with term-expiry years
tables.what_it_is: Every appointed committee, commission and single-officeholder post, with members and term expiry.
tables.grain: One person (or recorded vacancy) in one appointed role
tables.layout: Alphabetical by body; heading line gives size and term; single-column member list
tables.notes: Runs Agricultural Commission through Zoning Board of Appeals. Several headings are broken mid-word by the extractor ('PUBLIC A / CCESS CABLE COMMITTEE', 'TREE WARDE / N'). Personnel Committee is listed as '5 Vacancies'. One Green Communities term reads 'expires 20247'.

tables.name: Combining balance sheet, enterprise funds
tables.what_it_is: Unaudited combining balance sheet as of 30 June 2025 for the town's four enterprise funds, with a memorandum-only total column.
tables.grain: One balance-sheet line item across the enterprise funds
tables.layout: Line-item rows down the left, one money column per fund; column headings are stacked and appear at the TOP of the extracted page while the sheet's own title block ('Combining Balance Sheet - Enterprise Funds / as of June 30, 2025 / (unaudited) / TOWN OF LUNENBURG') is extracted at the BOTTOM
tables.notes: Two blank money columns sit between Peg Access and the Totals column — a spreadsheet artefact that will misalign a naive column split. The sheet carries its own Proof row, which is the check to reconcile to. Total Assets = 6,840,945.59; Total Liabilities = 3,212,453.64; Total Fund Equity = 3,628,491.95.

tables.name: Special revenue fund balance detail
tables.what_it_is: Every special revenue fund the town holds — school revolving accounts, gifts, grants, state and federal awards — with its closing balance and any remaining deficit. This is the most granular list of non-general-fund money in the book.
tables.layout: Four-column money table running continuously across four pages; column headings printed once on p26 only
tables.notes: Continues p26 -> p29 with NO repeated header. Fund names are truncated to ~10 characters by the source system ('SCH CHOICE', 'ARPAFUNDS', 'FY25117SOA'), so names are not self-explanatory. The middle column header says 'Receipts thru 9/30/2024' while the balance column says 6/30/2025 — the two columns are as-of different dates, which matters. Negative balances are shown in parentheses and repeated in the Deficits column. One entry (2672) spans two lines: 'FY26 Family & Community'. Fund 3107 on the following capital table has a number and no name or amount at all.

tables.name: Capital project fund balance detail
tables.what_it_is: Unspent balances remaining in each authorized capital project fund as of 30 June 2025.
tables.layout: Money table, top half of the page
tables.notes: Fund 3107 is printed with a number and nothing else — no name and no amount. Project names carry the town meeting that authorised them ('3101 FY22 Cap Plan #5 5/21 ATM'). Largest balances: FY25 Capital Plan $890,668.89, FY24 Capital Plan $829,034.00, FY22 Cap Plan $569,740.41.

tables.name: Trust fund balance detail
tables.what_it_is: Balance of every town trust and stabilization fund at 30 June 2025 plus receipts, including the Stabilization Fund, OPEB Trust, Opioid Settlement Stabilization and the scholarship trusts.
tables.grain: One numbered trust or stabilization fund
tables.layout: Money table starting mid-p30 and running to line 32 of p31
tables.notes: NO printed total for this table — it simply ends and the Undesignated Fund Balance Roll-forward heading follows on the same page. The receipts column header says 'Thru 9-30-2025', a date AFTER the fiscal year end and a year later than the equivalent column on the special-revenue table. Notable balances: Stabilization Fund $3,147,178.96; Vehicles/Equipment Stabilization $2,598,621.38; OPEB Trust $1,649,190.51; Conservation Trust $967,726.65; Opioid Settlement Stabilization $241,421.18; Dora Haven Cowdrey Scholarship $430,442.90. Ends with three non-8xxx accounts (9000 Regional Assessor, 9001 Police/Fire Special Detail, 9002 Custodian Special Detail).

tables.name: Undesignated fund balance roll-forward (free cash derivation)
tables.what_it_is: The add/deduct worksheet that carries last year's undesignated fund balance forward to this year's, through encumbrances, reservations, and revenue and expenditure closeouts.
tables.grain: One add or deduct line in the roll-forward
tables.layout: Single-column worksheet with Add:/Less:/Deduct: section markers; the answer lands alone at the top of p33
tables.printed_total: 4,236,488.24  (immediately followed by 'PROOF UNDESIGNATED FUND BALANCE AGREES TO THE BALANCE SHEET')
tables.notes: Roughly half the rows are blank placeholders ('Prior Year Reserved for' repeated with no label and no value) — these are template lines, not data. Key values: Beginning undesignated Fund Balance 2,751,841.80; Prior Year Reserved for Encumbrance 369,841.91; Prior Year Total Fund Balance 3,121,683.71; Current Year Reserved for Encumbrance 149,066.15; Current Reserved for Expenditures 1,540,424.00; Current Year Reserved for ATM ART #7 5/4/2025 ATM 458,966.86; Current Year Revenue Closeouts 3,288,261.54; Current Year Expenditure Closeouts 25,000.00. The label 'Current Year Undesignated Fund Balance' on p32 has its value printed on the next page. NOTE: the Town Manager's report on p22 states free cash was certified at $2,270,060, a different figure from this 4,236,488.24 — the two are different quantities (certified free cash vs undesignated fund balance) and must not be conflated.

tables.name: Assessed valuation by property class
tables.what_it_is: FY2025 total assessed valuation split into the four property classes with each class's share.
tables.layout: Small three-column table at the foot of the Board of Assessors narrative
tables.notes: Residential $2,161,060,074 (92%); Commercial $97,763,006 (4%); Industrial $32,627,700 (1%); Personal Property $69,258,000 (3%). The percentages sum to 100 only after rounding.

tables.name: Valuation year-over-year and average property values
tables.what_it_is: Prior-year total valuation and percent change, plus average single-family and average commercial/industrial value for FY2025 vs FY2024.
tables.grain: One property type compared across two fiscal years
tables.layout: Six lines occupying the whole (near-empty) page
tables.notes: FY2024 Total Valuation $2,242,686,580, % Change 5%. Avg. Single Family Value $504,937 vs $481,417 (5%). Avg. Commer/Indust. Value $435,910 vs $404,408 (7.7%). Last line reads 'FY2025 LA4/Assessment Clarification-Town of Lunenburg' — a source note naming the DOR LA4 form. The $504,937 average single-family value is the figure reused in every tax-impact calculation in the Finance Committee report.

tables.name: Treasurer's cash by bank account
tables.what_it_is: Every bank/investment account the Treasurer held at 30 June 2025 and its balance — named by institution and purpose.
tables.grain: One bank account or cash position
tables.layout: Two-column list, dollar sign printed AFTER the number
tables.notes: Several account names are shredded by the extractor into spaced-out characters ('E dwa rd Jo ne s L i bra ry T rus t F unds', 'Uni ba nk - Pa rk Re vo lvi ng F und'). Institutions named: Bartholomew, BlueStone, Edward Jones, Enterprise, Fidelity, Harbor One, Hometown, Main Street, MMDT, Newburyport, TD BankNorth, Unibank. This is the only place the book names the town's banking relationships.

tables.name: Trust funds investment activity (pooled portfolio)
tables.what_it_is: Full-year investment accounting for each named trust in the pooled portfolio: beginning market value, principal/earnings split, income, gains, transfers, ending balances and unrealized gain/loss.
tables.layout: Fourteen money columns on one landscape page, grouped into four sections (CEMETERY FUNDS, CONSERVATION FUNDS, SCHOLARSHIP FUNDS, MISCELLANEOUS FUNDS) each with a SUBTOTALS row, then GRAND TOTALS
tables.notes: The single hardest table in the book. Column headers are printed vertically/stacked and land as 24 separate lines at the top of the extracted page BEFORE any data. Data values run together with no space between them where a value is negative or where the fund name abuts the first number ('C. ALLEN HEADSTONE$409.32'). Four SUBTOTALS rows must be excluded from any per-fund sum. Page footer states 'ACCOUNTING METHOD : BOOK VALUE'. Cross-check: the ENDING CASH VALUE grand total $1,882,242.44 equals the 'Batholomew PrudentTrust Funds' line on the Treasurer's Cash page (p35).

tables.name: Five years outstanding debt
tables.printed_heading: FIVE YEARS OUTSTAND ING D EBT
tables.what_it_is: Principal outstanding by purpose for each of the last five fiscal years, split inside and outside the general debt limit, plus short-term debt.
tables.grain: One debt purpose across five years
tables.layout: Five year-columns; two sections (Inside / Outside the General Debt Limit) each with its own total, then long-term and short-term totals
tables.notes: Row labels are letter-spaced by the extractor ('L a nd Acqui si ti on', 'D epa r tmenta l E qui pment'). Schools debt outside the limit is $26,175,000 of the $28,400,000 outside-limit total and dominates the town's debt. Footnote printed on the page: '(1)Principal amount only. Excludes lease and installment purchase obligations, overlapping debt and unfunded pension liability.' The page ALSO carries the heading 'TRUST & STABILIZATION FUNDS HELD BY OTHER BANKS' at line 1 with no data whatsoever beneath it — see the surprises list.

tables.name: Authorized unissued debt and prospective financing
tables.printed_heading: Authorized Unissued Debt and Prospective Financing
tables.what_it_is: The list of purposes for which the town holds borrowing authorization it has not yet issued.
tables.layout: Two columns, twelve lines on an otherwise blank page
tables.notes: EVERY amount is a bare dash — the table lists eight purposes (School Feasibility Study Bond, School Construction, Land Acquisition, Sewer Construction x2, Pavement Management Plan, Artificial Turf Field & Track, Ladder Truck-Fire Department) with no dollar figures at all. An extractor will produce eight rows with a null amount; that is what the page actually says.

tables.name: Debt repayment schedule
tables.what_it_is: Principal, interest and (for MWPAT loans) admin fee due in each fiscal year from 2026 through 2047 for every outstanding issue, with a total column.
tables.grain: One component (PRINCIPAL / INTEREST / ADMIN FEE / issue subtotal) of one bond issue, across 22 fiscal years
tables.layout: 23 numeric columns on a single landscape page; each issue occupies 2-4 stacked rows (PRINCIPAL / INTEREST / [ADMIN FEE] / TOTAL <issue name>)
tables.notes: The header row is a single unspaced run: 'FISCAL YEAR2026202720282029...2047 TOTAL' — the years must be reconstructed by position, not read. Short rows (issues that mature early) have FEWER values than there are year columns, so column position cannot be inferred from value count; the extractor drops the leading empty cells. One interest row is split mid-number across two lines ('INTEREST$44,' / '875 $42,875 ...'). Also carries GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL ($31,576,807), GRAND TOTAL INTEREST ($11,201,102), GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL & INTEREST ($42,777,909) and GRAND TOTAL MWPAT ADMIN FEES ($7,012). Footnote: '*MASS WATER POLLUTION ABATEMENT TRUST: PAYMENT AMOUNTS TO BE SUBSIDIZED BY EQUITY EARNINGS AND CONTRACT ASSISTANCE PAYMENTS'. The two GOB MS-HS CONSTRUCTION issues together account for $31.2M of the $42.8M total.

tables.name: Collection of taxes receivables summary
tables.what_it_is: Receivable activity for FY2025 by tax type and levy year — what was carried forward, committed, abated, paid, refunded, transferred and adjusted, and what remains. Includes betterments, liens, tax title and sewer/water user charges.
tables.grain: One tax type and levy year (e.g. REAL ESTATE / LEVY OF 2015)
tables.layout: Eight money columns; section headings for REAL ESTATE, PERSONAL PROPERTY, MOTOR VEHICLE EXCISE, OTHER EXCISE TAXES, SUPPLEMENTAL TAXES, then unheaded blocks for liens/title/user charges/betterments; runs p40 -> p41
tables.notes: Row labels are letter-spaced ('L EVY OF 2007'). Most rows have values in only one or two of the eight columns, so a naive whitespace split assigns them to the wrong column — this table needs positional extraction. Header printed once, on p40 only. FY2025 real estate commitment is 32,933,027.21 and personal property 996,587.57; motor vehicle excise levy of 2025 commitment 1,745,393.70. Sewer betterment unapportioned assessments carry 2,787,311.53. Tax liens outstanding 1,214,126.02, foreclosures 47,179.26. Column heading is misspelled 'COMMITTMENTS' in the source.

tables.name: Building department permits issued
tables.what_it_is: Count of permits issued during FY25 by permit type.
tables.layout: Two-column table at the top of the page
tables.notes: Building 600, Demolition 10, Sheet Metal 35, Plumbing 166, Gas 140, Electrical 459. Sums to 1,410, matching the printed total. The word 'Total' is letter-spaced in the extract.

tables.name: Cemetery interments during the year
tables.what_it_is: Named list of every person interred in a Lunenburg town cemetery during 2025, with age, which cemetery, and whether the interment was a cremation. Some entries also note war service.
tables.layout: TWO side-by-side name/age/cemetery groups per line, organised by month (January-December); the month headings appear in both columns, so months interleave down the page
tables.notes: The page is a two-up month calendar: reading it line by line puts a May burial next to a November one. Sub-line 'List of people interred this year.' An asterisk before a name denotes cremation ('*Denotes Cremations'), and the total block itself is broken across three lines. Long names wrap to a second line with no age or cemetery ('*Miriam Cheesman' / 'MacKenna' / '(WWII)'). Some cemetery values are plot references rather than names ('N/W East #60', 'N/W East #58'). War-service notes in parentheses: (Vietnam) x2, (Korean), (WWII). The DPW report on p51 independently repeats '31 cremations and 7 full burials were performed this year'.

tables.name: Conservation Commission filing counts
tables.what_it_is: Counts of wetlands filings acted on during the fiscal year, stated inside a narrative sentence rather than as a table.
tables.layout: Prose sentence
tables.notes: Verbatim: 'During this period the Conservation Commission supported 28 NOIs, 36 Administrative Determinations, 18 RDAs, 34 COCs, and numerous other requests.' Note the same paragraph calls the period 'fiscal year 2025-26'.

tables.name: Council on Aging participation and volunteer statistics
tables.what_it_is: Volunteer count and hours, unique participants and units of service at the Adult Activity Center for FY25, given in prose.
tables.layout: Prose
tables.notes: 42 volunteers, 668 hours; approximately 1,184 people used the Center; those 1,184 compiled 22,871 'units of duplicated service'. Note that 'units of duplicated service' is an activity count, not a headcount.

tables.name: Chapter 70 aid and foundation enrollment, FY13-FY26
tables.what_it_is: Fourteen-year history of Lunenburg's foundation enrollment and Chapter 70 aid with year-over-year percent changes, printed inside the Finance Committee report.
tables.layout: Five-column table mid-page; the 'Enrollment' half of the first column heading wraps to a second line
tables.notes: FY13 through FY26. This is the single most reusable financial time series in the book. FY25 = 1,615 enrollment / $8,988,960 aid / 1.9%; FY26 = 1,633 / $9,109,185 / 1.3%. The surrounding text states aid grew 5.3%/yr FY13-FY23 and 1.5%/yr in the last three years. FY26 figures are the Governor's budget, not final — the text says so.

tables.name: FY26 budget and override figures in the Finance Committee report
tables.what_it_is: The levy-limit build-up, state aid estimate, school appropriation, override and debt-exclusion amounts and their per-household tax impacts, all embedded in narrative rather than tabulated.
tables.layout: Prose with bulleted article summaries
tables.notes: Key figures: FY25 Levy Limit $31,602,108; automatic 2.5% increase $790,052.70; new growth estimate $400,000; total increase 3.76%; excluded debt $2,213,677; maximum allowable levy $35,005,838. FY2026 Net State Aid estimated $10,006,739; Chapter 70 $9,109,185. School Department $25,787,474 in the Omnibus Budget, requiring elimination of ~28 FTE (39 employees). Citizens petition override $2,099,337 = +$0.89/$1,000 = +$449/yr on a $504,937 home = 6.19%. Marshall Park $13.8M = +$0.46/$1,000 = +$231 = 3.2%. Municipal Building $21.4M-$22.3M = +$0.57/$1,000 = +$288 = 3.97%. Chapter 90 rising from $418,227 to $690,000. Health insurance +14.84%. Regular debt decreasing $393,881.14, redirected to FY26 Capital ($244,576) and operating offsets ($149,305). Debt policy limits: regular <4%, excludable <11%, combined <14%.

tables.name: Library FY2025 usage statistics
tables.what_it_is: Headline library counts for the year: visitors, programs and attendance, physical and electronic circulation, meeting room use.
tables.layout: Five label: value lines
tables.notes: Visitors 68,459 (4% increase); Programming 410 events with 6,759 attendees; Physical Circulations 77,543; Electronic Circulations 34,363 (29% increase); Meeting Rooms Used by Community 1,181 times. Library trust funds total $104,808.21 as of June 27, 2025 ($63,848.09 at Edward Jones, $36,000 in a brokered CD), up 7.6%; no trust funds spent this year.

tables.name: Library department-level program and collection counts
tables.what_it_is: Adult, Young Adult and Children's Services counts scattered through bulleted narrative — programs, attendance, summer reading registrations and minutes read, collection sizes and circulation.
tables.layout: Bulleted prose under Adult Services / Young Adult Services / Children's Services headings
tables.notes: Adult: 182 programs, 2,067 attendees; 71 digital resources. Teen: 48 events / 285 participants; 57 teens signed up for summer reading with 73,172 minutes logged; 14 homeschool events / 206 participants. Children: 229 summer reading registrants, 222,000 minutes; 640 free lunches in July; 32 Little Listeners + 34 Preschool Story Times reaching 1,761 children; 28 STEM kits circulating 75 times; graphic novel collection 820 items circulating 5,000+ times. Almost 400 people registered for summer reading overall; ~650 lunches served.

tables.name: Public Access Cable revenue vs expenses
tables.what_it_is: The PEG Access enterprise fund's FY25 income sources, total expenses and beginning/ending balance.
tables.layout: Small two-column block; labels wrap onto their own lines
tables.notes: Revenue (from Comcast) $180,792; Enterprise Fund Interest $46,343; Investment Interest $35,430; Subtotal $262,565; Expenses $178,140; Beginning Balance $208,772; Ending Balance $30,632. Comcast revenue fell 6.3% from $192,954. Note the arithmetic: 208,772 + 262,565 - 178,140 does not equal 30,632, so the block is not a simple roll-forward.

tables.name: Public Access Cable expenses by line item
tables.printed_heading: FY25 LINE ITEMS AS A PERCENTAGE

tables.notes: Salaries $98,868.97 (55.50%); Videographers $37,512.50 (21.06%); Indirect Costs $27,929.97 (15.68%); Equip/Maint $7,156.03 (4.02%); Lease $6,000.00 (3.37%); Purchase of Services $633.50 (0.36%); Consultant $40.00 (0.02%); Office Supls, Advertising, New Equip, Vendor Expenses all $0.00. The Total row is on the FOLLOWING page from the data. The pie-chart labels on p61-62 and p65 are truncated by the extractor ('Entertainme…Informati…', 'Even…') and their underlying percentages (Informational 31%, Events 25%, Entertainment 32%) are given only in the p61 narrative.

tables.name: Senior property tax work-off program
tables.what_it_is: The program's eligibility rules and rates plus the year's participation: how many residents, in which departments, for how many hours and how much abatement.
tables.grain: One eligibility rule / one participating department
tables.layout: Bulleted eligibility list on p66; participation paragraph and department bullet list on p67
tables.printed_total: These individuals as a whole, accumulated 293.75 hours amounting to $4,406.25, before deductions, in real estate tax abatements.
tables.notes: Period stated as JANUARY 1, 2025 – NOVEMBER 1, 2025 (a calendar-year window, not the fiscal year). 2025 abatement maximum $1,500, hourly rate $15.00, applied to the 3rd quarter real estate bill. Income limits: one person $50,000, two person $75,000. Six residents participated, across Council on Aging, Public Library, Tax Collector, Assessors and Sewer — five departments listed for six people.

tables.name: Sewer system operating statistics
tables.what_it_is: Connection counts, billing, delinquency, pump-station repair costs and the FY26 sewer articles, in narrative.
tables.layout: Prose
tables.notes: 1,226 properties connected; 270 with access but not connected; 14 new connections in FY25. Billed $1,187,341.09 in quarterly sewer bills; $67,187.77 moved to December 2024 tax bills for non-payment; delinquency rate averaging 18%. ~89% of sewage discharged to Leominster, 11% to Fitchburg; ten pump stations. Mass 1 pump station repair $98,000 (completed Nov 2024); Dana Street $123,600 (scheduled June 2025). $100,000 ARPA for manhole I/I repairs. FY26 sewer budget article: $1,886,150.22 appropriated from $1,583,917.45 anticipated receipts plus $302,232.77 retained earnings.

tables.name: Veterans' services Chapter 115 caseload and payments
tables.what_it_is: Number of Chapter 115 benefit recipients at the start and end of FY25, total benefits paid and the state reimbursement.
tables.layout: Prose paragraph
tables.notes: Started FY25 serving 5 recipients, ended serving 7 per month. Paid out $50,323.27, averaging $4,193.61/month; reimbursed $38,283.61 by the state, described as 'the maximum allowable 75% share'. 38,283.61 / 50,323.27 = 76.1%, so the 75% description and the figures do not tie exactly.

tables.name: Nashoba Associated Boards of Health service counts
tables.what_it_is: Counts of inspections, permits, applications and reviews the regional health agent performed for Lunenburg, given as parenthetical numbers in section headings and inside sentences.
tables.layout: Section headings carrying a count in parentheses, plus counts embedded in paragraphs
tables.notes: Food Service Licensing and Inspections (64); Recreational Permitting and Inspections (11); Housing & Nuisance Investigation (27). Title 5: 83 soil-testing applications, 158 tests witnessed, 49 sewage disposal system applications, 32 plans reviewed, 34 permits prepared (15 new construction, 19 replacement of failed systems), 92 construction inspections, 86 Title 5 inspection reports reviewed. Private wells: 17 permits. The counts in parentheses are district-wide vs town-specific in places — the text does not always say which.

tables.name: Communicable disease cases investigated
tables.printed_heading: Communicable Disease Number of Cases investigated:
tables.what_it_is: Count of each reportable disease investigated by the Nashoba nursing team.
tables.layout: Leader-dotted two-column list
tables.notes: Calicivirus/Norovirus 5; Hepatitis C 1; Human Granulocytic Anaplasmosis 4; Influenza 136; Novel Coronavirus (SARS, MERS, etc) 59; Salmonellosis 1; Streptococcus pneumoniae 1. tables.name: Fire department calls for service by category

tables.printed_total: In 2025, your Fire Department responded to 2006 calls for service

tables.name: Fire department roster
tables.printed_heading: Roster of the Lunenburg Fire Department- 2025
tables.what_it_is: Every member of the fire department by name and rank/certification, split into career staff by shift and call firefighters.

Legend printed on the page: '*Indicates member of District Technical Rescue Team; + Indicates Career/Full Time Staff; FF- Firefighter; EMT- Firefighter/Emergency Medical Technician - Basic; AEMT- Advanced Emergency Medical Technician'. Roughly 11 career/admin and 29 call firefighters.

tables.name: Police department personnel roster
tables.what_it_is: Every sworn and civilian member of the police department by assignment.

tables.notes: Columns interleave badly in the text dump — e.g. 'K9 Ofc. John Wagner Bureau Ofc. Robert DaCosta' merges three different columns. One Sergeant post is printed as 'Sgt. Vacant'. The SRO entry carries a parenthetical '(Accompanied by Comfort Dog: Hank)' split across two lines and two columns.

tables.name: Police department activity statistics, 2024 vs 2025
tables.what_it_is: Calls for service, arrests, motor vehicle activity, crime types, mental health incidents and firearms licensing, each compared between 2024 and 2025.
tables.grain: One activity type across two calendar years
tables.layout: Three-column table beginning at the foot of p80 and continuing to line 32 of p81 with no repeated header
tables.notes: Continues across the page break WITHOUT a repeated header — the p81 rows have no column labels. Calendar-year data, not fiscal. Calls for Service fell 22,880 -> 18,822 while Arrests Total rose 315 -> 435 and Citations Criminal Offenses rose 120 -> 381. Sub-rows are indented under parents (Arrests Total / Custody / Summons; MVA Total / w-Injury / w-o Injury / Hit & Run; Firearms Licensing / LTC / FID / Over 70 / License to Sell / Machine gun) so summing all rows double-counts. tables.name: Trust Fund Commission FY2025 annual report
tables.printed_heading: TRUST FUND COMMISSION –ANNUAL REPORT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2025
tables.what_it_is: The newly seated Trust Fund Commission's own report on trust fund values — covering only the quarter ending 31 March 2025, because that is the only data it was given.
tables.grain: One fund category or named fund
tables.layout: Bulleted label: value lists under all-caps section headings
tables.notes: This report contradicts the Treasurer's own Trust Funds statement on p36, and says so: it reports a GRAND TOTAL of $1,454,369.67 at 3/31/2025 where p36 reports an ENDING MARKET VALUE of $2,155,276.15 at fiscal year end. It reports total FY25 interest/investment income of $427.93 where p36 reports NET INCOME of $38,380.98. The commission states plainly why: 'All available FY25 financial data originates from the Town of Lunenburg Trust Funds quarterly report for the period ending March 31, 2025', 'Only one quarter (ending 3/31/2025) was available for FY25', and 'No FY25 portfolio holdings document was included; therefore, investment range data cannot be reported.' It closes with a DISCLAIMER inviting an addendum. The named miscellaneous funds it lists (American Legion Poor $12,489.53; J & M Howard SDWLK/GRDS $22,211.58; Worthy Poor Income $22,887.22; Gazebo Restoration $10,725.46; Lunenburg Post #283 $8,690.14) are the same five funds as the MISCELLANEOUS FUNDS section on p36, at a different date. The report also has a 'QUARTERLY PERFORMANCE MATRIX' heading with no matrix under it.

surprises: There is NO town-wide revenue or receipts table of any kind. Earlier years' 'SUMMARY OF RECEIPTS' has no successor here under any name. I checked every page and grepped for receipt/revenue/recapitulation/local receipts. What exists instead is scattered: a 'Receipts thru 9/30/2024' column inside the special revenue fund detail (p26-29), a single 'Current Year Revenue Closeouts 3,288,261.54' line in the fund balance roll-forward (p32), a 14-year Chapter 70 aid series in the Finance Committee report (p53), the PEG Access enterprise fund's own revenue block (p64), and the tax COMMITMENTS column of the receivables summary (p40-41). The revenue side of the general fund is simply not published in this book.

A section heading with no section under it: 'TRUST & STABILIZATION FUNDS HELD BY OTHER BANKS' is printed at the top of PDF p37, is listed in the table of contents as printed page 33, and has no data beneath it at all — the Five Years Outstanding Debt table starts immediately. Either the table was dropped in layout or it exists only as an untagged image.

The Trust Fund Commission's own report (p184-185) openly contradicts the Treasurer's trust fund statement (p36) and explains why: the Commission was only ever given one quarter of FY25 data. Two different grand totals for the same portfolio ($1,454,369.67 vs $2,155,276.15) sit 148 pages apart in the same document, and only the later one flags the problem.

Three of the four school staff rosters run onto a second page that carries NO heading (Primary p101, THES p103, LMS p106, LHS p110). Searching for 'STAFF ROSTER' finds four pages and misses roughly 140 of the roughly 230 named school staff — most of the paraprofessionals, therapists, custodians, cafeteria and grade-level teams are on the unheaded continuation pages.

The Special Services report (p92) publishes the out-of-district placement COUNT and its breakdown — 10 students, of whom 6 collaborative, 3 day, 1 residential (up from 8 last year) — sourced to the March 1, 2025 SIMS Report 7. That is the quantity the town's budget documents never give.
The Fire Department's own call breakdown does not add up: 387 + 1233 + 320 + 29 = 1,969 against a stated 2,006 calls, on the same page (p75).
The Annual Town Election tally sheet contains an arithmetic error: SAMUEL E. SMITH's precinct votes (80, 75, 54, 107) sum to 316 but the printed TOTAL is 209 (p171).
Registered voters are stated twice and differ: 9,240 in the Lunenburg Profile (p9) and 9,608 on the official election tally sheet (p171).
The town's own Appointed Officials page names Barbara Reynolds as Lunenburg's Monty Tech representative (p16); Monty Tech's own committee list names Stephanie Quinn for Lunenburg (p133).
'Authorized Unissued Debt and Prospective Financing' (p38) lists eight borrowing purposes and a dash in every single amount cell — the table is structurally complete and numerically empty.

The Article 7 deficit table asks for $415,000 for Snow & Ice but the motion as voted transferred $408,966.86 — and the difference, $458,966.86, reappears as a reserved line in the fund balance roll-forward (p32) labelled 'Current Year Reserved for ATM ART #7 5/4/2025 ATM'.
Full enrollment by vocational program exists for all 21 Monty Tech shops, but only as a parenthetical at the end of each narrative paragraph (p120-125), never as a table.

The report is dated FY2025 but a great deal of it is written from a February 2026 vantage: school enrollments are 'as of February 2026', athletic results run into the 2025-26 winter season, the Sewer Commission signs off 'as of report submittal (Feb 2026)', and the Conservation Commission describes 'fiscal year 2025-26'. Calendar-year and fiscal-year data are mixed throughout without labelling — police statistics, fire calls, cemetery interments, vitals and gross wages are all calendar 2025.

Free cash appears as two different numbers with no reconciliation between them: the Town Manager reports it 'certified at $2,270,060' (p22) while the Accountant's roll-forward lands on an undesignated fund balance of $4,236,488.24 (p33).

Six boards filed no report at all and the table of contents says so in the contents itself: Cultural Council, Green Communities Committee, Historical Commission, Housing Authority, Capital Planning Report, and the Master Planning Steering Committee. Capital Planning filing nothing is notable given the Capital Plan tables that appear under Article 8.
